questions.q: What model does Nagoski use to explain sexual arousal?
a: A gas pedal and brakes
A light switch and dimmer
A thermostat and radiator
An engine and steering wheel
questions.why: Lesson 1 says stimulation presses the gas pedal, while many things can press the brakes and shut desire down.

questions.q: What do most people who struggle with sex have, according to the summary?
a: Overactive sexual brakes
A weak stress response
An unusually strong gas pedal
A hormonal imbalance
questions.why: The summary says most people who struggle simply have brakes that are too sensitive or too easily triggered.

questions.q: What should you do when you feel stressed, according to the summary?
a: Calm down first through exercise, sleep or affection
Push through and have sex anyway
Wait for the stress to disappear on its own
Avoid all physical contact until it passes
questions.why: Lesson 2 advises completing the stress response first, through exercise, sleep, crying, affection or relaxation.

questions.q: Why can't we simply decide to switch off stress?
a: The stress response cycle cannot be turned off at will
Stress only affects animals, not people
Stress hormones fade within seconds
The brain ignores stress once sex begins
questions.why: The summary compares humans to animals playing dead and says the stress cycle keeps running after the threat is gone.

questions.q: How does the media damage people's sex lives, according to the summary?
a: It makes them feel inadequate and pressured to perform
It teaches techniques that frequently injure partners
It reduces the time couples spend together
It exposes children to adult content too early
questions.why: Lesson 3 says media messages make people self-conscious and suggest they must agree to every sexual activity.
